Rootogram of observed and expected count frequencies

Source: R/diagnostics.R
rootogram.Rd

Draws a hanging rootogram (Kleiber and Zeileis, 2016). The square roots of the expected frequencies from expected_counts() form a curve, and a bar for each observed frequency hangs from it. A bar that stops above the zero line marks a count the model over-predicts. A bar that crosses below it marks a count the model under-predicts.

Usage

rootogram(object, max_count = NULL, ...)

Arguments

object

An nbreg or zinbreg fit.

max_count

Largest count to show; see expected_counts().

...

Graphical arguments for graphics::plot(), such as main, xlab, ylab, xlim or ylim. They replace the defaults.

Value

The table from expected_counts(), invisibly.

Details

The counts 0 to max_count are drawn. The grouped last row of expected_counts() is left out of the plot but kept in the returned table. The plot uses base graphics.

Errors and warnings

As for expected_counts(). Arguments in ... go to graphics::plot(), which reports its own errors.

References

Kleiber, C. and Zeileis, A. (2016). Visualizing count data regressions using rootograms. The American Statistician, 70(3), 296-303.

See also

expected_counts()

Examples

set.seed(1)
d <- data.frame(x = rnorm(200))
d$y <- ifelse(runif(200) < 0.3, 0, rnbinom(200, size = 2, mu = exp(1 + d$x)))
rootogram(nbreg(y ~ x, data = d), max_count = 10)

rootogram(zinbreg(y ~ x | 1, data = d), max_count = 10)
